A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 10-page versions of the CodeBrain research work. Their text, equations, tables and figures support comparison despite substantial revisions. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: V2 reports original MRI imputation experiments on IXI and BraTS 2023, component ablations, and downstream tumour segmentation results.

after.justification: V3 reports original imputation and segmentation results on both datasets, including revised comparisons and additional loss and conditioning experiments.

M1.justification: V2 encodes a randomly selected anchor modality and reconstructs that modality; v3 encodes the concatenated complete modality set and reconstructs all modalities jointly. Accordingly, Stage II predicts a joint code map rather than concatenated separately encoded modality codes. Section 3 also replaces the anchor reconstruction objective with full-set PSNR reconstruction weighted differently for missing and available modalities.

E1.justification: Both versions use healthy-subject IXI data with T1, T2 and PD, and BraTS 2023 tumour data with T1, T2, FLAIR and T1Gd. Both evaluate one-to-one and many-to-one imputation and four three-to-one segmentation scenarios. V3's BraTS visual examples remain within this existing coverage; virtual full-stack scanning does not introduce a separate acquisition experiment.

E2.justification: In Table 2, v3 removes MMSYN, adds Zhang et al. and MMHVAE, and retains MMGAN, MMT and M2DN. Zhang et al. was cited but not evaluated there in v2. The segmentation comparison in Table 4 separately removes M2DN and adds Zhang et al. and MMHVAE while retaining MMT.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 changes IXI registration from rigid registration to T2 to SyNRA, Adam at 1e-3 to AdamW at 1e-4, and 250 to 300 epochs per stage. Uniform L=5 with d=9/7 becomes L=[8,8,8,5,5,5] with d=6. Table 4 changes paired 2D/3D Dice reporting to mean 3D Dice over three tumour regions. Split counts remain unchanged; these reported protocol revisions prevent direct same-setting performance comparisons.

E4.justification: Common-feature and grading ablations remain, but v2's joint d=5/7/9 sweep becomes a single-configuration table. Explicit-VQ comparisons disappear, while v3 compares binary, two FSQ capacities and continuous conditions. V3 adds L1-versus-PSNR loss and reconstruction-weight analyses, removes the segmentation-prediction agreement control, and extends code-map case studies to BraTS.

E5.justification: The reported random seed changes from 1234 to 1334. V3 Figure 6 introduces box-and-whisker PSNR displays, whereas v2 provides point-value bars and tables. Their sampling unit and whisker definitions are unspecified, so they cannot establish repeated-run uncertainty. Neither version documents repeated-run counts or a confidence-interval procedure.

E6.justification: Main comparisons, reconstruction results, segmentation scores and ablation outcomes are substantially replaced or expanded. Table 2 reports CodeBrain mean PSNR of 29.43/25.16 dB on IXI/BraTS in v2 and 29.50/25.31 in v3; the IXI runner-up changes from MMT to Zhang et al. These are results under revised methods and settings, not established same-setting gains. Table 4 also replaces the segmentation results and removes the prediction-as-label entries.

T1.justification: Section 3 generalizes the quantizer and codebook definition from uniform L and L^d to channel-specific Li and their product, and revises the formal reconstruction objective. The ordinal binary encoding and straight-through estimator retain their underlying principles; no theorem or proof is added. The new even-valued quantization settings introduce a cardinality inconsistency in the written formula.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion refine the representation claim from modality- and instance-specific codes to a joint, region-level representation of the complete modality set that models cross-modality relationships. The overarching claims of unified any-to-any imputation, two-stage scalar-code prediction with grading, superior imputation and downstream segmentation benefit remain.

C2.justification: Section 4.4 adds interpretation of the PSNR-versus-SSIM loss trade-off and benefits over fixed binary conditioning. It removes interpretations tied to the explicit-VQ and d-sweep experiments and the assertion of superior 3D consistency despite 2D training. The hallucination limitation remains, with 3D modelling newly proposed as a remedy alongside MRI physics.

D1.justification: The documented implementation recipe is substantially revised, including optimizer, learning rate, code configuration, training duration and software versions. Runtime changes from approximately 84 hours to 2.38 days. V3 supplies a specific planned code-release repository but omits v2's parameter/MAC counts, cosine-scheduler specification, explicit float-metric/data-range instructions and BraTS download link. The repository statement still promises future release rather than establishing availability.

R1.justification: Related work adds MMHVAE, autoregressive brain MRI synthesis, newer latent-diffusion and adaptive-interaction approaches, and quantization works including BSQ and Infinity. MMSYN and MAGVIT discussions are removed. These are substantive literature updates within the retained MRI-imputation and latent-quantization positioning; publication-metadata updates alone do not count.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction and much of the method narrative are extensively rewritten around virtual full-stack scanning and region-level code prediction. Method subsection titles and discussion organization change, limitations move from the conclusion to the discussion, and acknowledgements are added. The author and affiliation block also changes.

P2.justification: Figures 1 and 2 are substantially redrawn. Table 2 is transposed and gains colour highlighting; Figure 3 adds per-example PSNR annotations. Comparative images and code maps are replaced and reorganized, including BraTS examples. V2's multi-panel ablation bars become a compact table, while v3 adds a loss-weight table and conditioning boxplots and restructures the segmentation table.

improvement.justification: V3 improves presentation and adds evaluated comparators and targeted loss/conditioning evidence. However, it removes explicit-VQ and segmentation-agreement controls and several reproducibility details. It also introduces an unresolved specification issue: Equation (1), round(floor(Li/2) times tanh(F)), permits nine integers when Li=8, contradicting the stated eight levels and 64,000-code cardinality. The PDFs do not establish whether this is only a formula omission or affects implementation. These competing gains and losses prevent a reliable net quality judgment; revised protocols also preclude treating higher scores as proof of improvement.
